target.projectDescription: pgAdmin 4: a PostgreSQL administration tool. The server side is a Python Flask web application (web/pgadmin) with per-module blueprints, SQLAlchemy storage, and a Flask-SocketIO endpoint (/pty namespace) that backs the server-side psql terminal tool. It provides server registration/connection management (including per-server password-exec hooks), pg utility execution (backup/restore/maintenance/import_export) through a background BatchProcess/process_executor pipeline, cloud instance deployment (pgacloud), and a desktop runtime mode launched from web/pgAdmin4.py. User-facing requests, socket messages, preferences, and config all reach these command-execution features.

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: Attackers face (1) the Flask HTTP surface: 269 blueprint routes whose handlers read request.data (220 sites), request.form (185), request.args (101), request.get_json (8), request.cookies/headers/environ (4/6/4) and json.loads(request...) bodies; (2) the Flask-SocketIO /pty namespace: six socket event handlers in web/pgadmin/tools/psql/__init__.py receive client message payloads (db, sid, pwd, user, input, rows, cols) and start a psql pty process; (3) the preferences/config surface: user-stored binary paths and config values (config.py patched by PGADMIN_CONFIG_* environment variables via evaluate_config.py); (4) server registration data including per-server passexec_cmd password-exec hook commands stored through the browser server API; (5) CLI entry points (web/setup.py argparse, pgacloud/pgacloud.py argparse). Command-execution sinks are subprocess.Popen/run/getoutput (three of them with shell=True or a Windows shell=True toggle), bare from-imported Popen call sites in the BatchProcess/process_executor pipeline, and the pty/winpty spawn in the psql tool.

inputBoundaryInventory.nonVulnerabilityNote: Predefined utility execution (backup/restore/maintenance/import_export via pg_dump/pg_restore/vacuum etc.), the cloud deployment pipeline, the psql terminal feature, and the passexec/master-password hooks are the product's intended command features. They are recorded as sink candidates for labeling only; none is presumed vulnerable, and no rule was added from any known vulnerability location.

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query compile, then sequential codeql query run (one at a time) and codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF (deferred to Phase 2)
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist). Raw BQRS output decodes directly to CSV.
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, -1 when not applicable)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs (API::moduleImport(...).getMember(...).getACall()); alias-aware, only genuine resolved calls into external modules (json.loads, os.getenv, subprocess.*, os.popen)
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic module prefix, receiver name, decorator shapes); catches the eventlet.green subprocess import, the from-imported bare Popen names, Flask request proxy reads, @blueprint.route / @sio.on handler signatures, and other dynamic or unresolved shapes. Subject to name-collision noise; both spellings of the request object alias (request / req / request_object) are matched explicitly

exclusions: web/regression/ (feature test harness) and all */tests/ directories are excluded from candidate rows via file-path filters in both queries
repo-root tools/ dev scripts (get_chromedriver.py, dependency_inventory.py, ...) are excluded via the same path filter
web/pgadmin/utils/driver/psycopg3/generate_keywords.py is NOT excluded (it lives outside tests/) but is a static dev codegen script; its os.popen rows are expected to be labeled none/low-relevance
pure logging/output helpers are not extracted

uncoveredCases: eventlet.green subprocess: pgadmin/tools/psql/__init__.py:15 'from eventlet.green import subprocess' - API graphs may resolve subprocess.Popen through the module alias or may not; the AST-shape match (module prefix 'subprocess') guarantees the site is captured either way, with match_kind recording which mechanism produced the row

bare from-imported execution names: 'from subprocess import call' (pgadmin/utils/javascript/javascript_bundler.py:12, call at :63) is not matched because a bare 'call' name is too collision-prone; bare Popen/system/popen/getoutput/getstatusoutput/check_output/check_call are matched. This is the only known bare-call execution site in non-test code

dynamic shell flag: pgadmin/misc/bgprocess/process_executor.py:324 'kwargs['shell'] = True if _IS_WIN else False' builds the shell flag through a dict at runtime; it is not a literal shell=True keyword, so it is documented here instead of producing a shell_true row
attribute-argument indirection: process_executor.py:330 'Popen(command, ..., **kwargs)' passes the shell flag via **kwargs; the Popen call itself is still captured as an arg row

request-object aliases: 'request as req' (file_manager) and the request_object parameter convention (browser get_delete_data helpers) are matched by explicit name list; any other alias spelling would be missed
flask proxy resolution: request is a werkzeug local proxy, so request.<field> reads never resolve through API graphs; they are AST-only rows by design

data['key'] subscripts on socket payloads (data['db'], data['input'], ...) inside @sio.on handlers are not individually extracted; the handler 'data' parameter rows plus the handler function names carry the boundary

CLI option attribute reads (args.<attr> / options.<attr> after parse_args) are not extracted because the bare names 'args'/'options' are heavily reused for non-CLI values in this codebase (e.g. backup args lists); argparse registration/parse calls and sys.argv are captured instead
BatchProcess.start() method invocations are receiver-typed only at runtime; the constructor call sites (exec_boundary rows) and the internal wrapper functions cover the boundary instead

schema/DB-stored values (Server.passexec_cmd, Process.command/arguments from the SQLAlchemy store) are reached through attribute reads on ORM query results; only the direct construction and consumption sites are captured, not the ORM round-trip
